"Hatzic" on this page is THREE governments under one board label - Hatzic Bench = City of Mission (Ferguson Avenue, Jasper Avenue, McEwen Avenue, Ferndale Avenue, Dewdney Trunk Road) — City bylaws, zoning and taxes apply, including the City's flat 10% tax penalty after July 2. - Hatzic Prairie = FVRD Electoral Area F — FVRD and Province rules, rural taxes paid to the Province (5% after July 2 + further 5% after October 31). - Hatzic Island = FVRD Electoral Area G (Shook Road addresses around Hatzic Lake and Hatzic Island) — FVRD and Province rules, rural taxes, not City bylaws and not Mission's flat 10%. The FVRD's Electoral Areas Housing Needs Report lists "Electoral Area F: McConnell Creek, Hatzic Prairie" and "Electoral Area G: Nicomen Island, Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island," and states the Hatzic Valley includes the historic settlement areas of Hatzic Prairie, Durieu, Miracle Valley and McConnell Creek. All of it carries "Mission" mailing addresses and sits in the board's Hatzic sub-area — a reporting grouping only. The tax regime follows the jurisdiction the parcel sits in, not the mailing address.

items.t: Every first-page card is labelled board sub-area "Hatzic" with a "Mission" mailing address, but the streets split into two different worlds: Bench streets inside the city (Ferguson Avenue, Jasper Avenue, McEwen Avenue, Ferndale Avenue, Dewdney Trunk Road) and Shook Road addresses around Hatzic Lake and Hatzic Island.
FVRD Prairie and Island ground has no SnapStats coverage of its own — no figure is quoted for it.

City planning frame (Bench only): the City of Mission's Official Community Plan is Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025 with the same vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction, with a Regional Context Statement added. This City frame does not govern the FVRD parts of the page; FVRD official community plan and zoning bylaws govern Areas F and G, with the specific bylaw numbers and zone names for a given Prairie/Island lot to be confirmed with the FVRD for the PID.

items.t: Secondary suites, two frames on one page: inside the City (Bench only), all secondary suites must be registered with the City, a suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity, and suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes. In FVRD Electoral Area F (Prairie), secondary suites are freely permitted with no restrictions related to farm use, but must be located within the principal dwelling and could not be a separate detached structure such as a garden suite. Which frame applies depends on which side of the City/FVRD line the parcel sits on.

ALR housing and stratification rules: the majority of the inhabited Hatzic Valley is in the ALR. On ALR parcels the housing frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; a strata plan deposit is a subdivision — Strata Property Act s. 239; ALR subdivision needs Commission permission — Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)).

blocks.text: Good to know about Hatzic

items.t: The mailing address lies about who governs you — on two-thirds of this page. Every listing here carries a Mission mailing address, yet a Ferguson Avenue house pays City taxes under City bylaws while a Shook Road property on Hatzic Island or in Hatzic Prairie is FVRD/Province ground with rural taxes (due July 2; 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31). A buyer who budgets Mission's flat 10% for a Prairie or Island parcel has the wrong regime — and vice versa.

Three tenures sit within one feed page at overlapping prices. A fee-simple Bench house, an Everglades undivided-interest seasonal lot and a Green Acres pad home are three different assets with different financing, seasonal-use and resale structures — tenure, park/resort rules and any seasonal-use limit must come from the park's or resort's own documents, not the listing card.
The one 55+ product here comes with an unsettled tax line. Mission Mobile Home Park's listings state 55+ outright.

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default on the Bench and the Prairie: the Bench houses (Ferguson Avenue and Jasper Avenue, an estate on 5.66 acres on Ferndale Avenue) and the Prairie acreages trade as whole fee-simple parcels unless title says otherwise — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. Lot sizes and zones are stated only as the sources state them (the 5.66-acre figure is listing-card text).

Not fee-simple land — Everglades Resort, 8400 Shook Road (Hatzic Lake, Island side): undivided-interest seasonal use holding: Fresh listings in the condos pass record Type Recreational / Land, describe a gated resort with clubhouse, playground, two boat launches and beach area, and state "No year round living"; one unit's record states Title to Land: Undivided Interest.

Not fee-simple land — Green Acres Mobile Park, Shook Road (Hatzic Lake): pad rental: The buyer owns the manufactured home and rents the pad under the MHPTA; there is no strata corporation and no Form B. A fresh listing states "Park approval is required" (listing text); no age rule is stated in any listing checked.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the FVRD records that the majority of the inhabited Hatzic Valley area is within the ALR, with active commercial and hobby farming alongside sparse residential uses — but no parcel-level split is published and none is stated; a specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID.

items.t: One page, three governments, two tax calendars. A Ferguson Avenue house pays City taxes with a flat 10% penalty after July 2; a Shook Road property on the Island or in the Prairie pays the Province at 5% + 5% (July 2 / October 31). Budgeting either regime for the other ground is simply wrong.

The cheapest "land" on the page is not land. Everglades use-areas and Green Acres pads sit in the same $229,000–$415,000 card range as real product on the first page, but they are a seasonal undivided interest and a pad tenancy — different financing, seasonal-use and resale structures from a fee-simple Bench lot.

Suites run on two different rulebooks on one page. City suites must be registered and are barred in townhouses/rowhomes; Area F suites must sit inside the principal dwelling with no detached garden-suite route. The PID's side of the line decides which book applies.

The West Coast Express does not serve the lake. It runs from Mission City Station in the City (five weekday westbound trains, 75 minutes to Waterfront, no weekend service); no transit summary for the lake, Island or Prairie was opened.
